summary: FINAL VERIFICATION PASSED — Step 7 alphabetical default is now persisted SERVER-SIDE via the top-level `step7_alpha_seeded` flag on the analysis doc, fully replacing the previous localStorage approach. All 7 primary/cross-device assertions (a–g) plus the 9 regression assertions from iteration_5 verified on mobile viewport 390x844 against analysis id=goals-feels-tracker. Reset to fresh state via API (PUT /config {step7_alpha_seeded:false} + POST /factors/reorder with reverse-alphabetical [Zeta,Mango,Echo,Banana,Alpha]), then loaded the wizard with localStorage cleared (only session_token preserved for auth). The Step 7 useEffect at /app/frontend/app/tools/pros-cons-wizard.tsx:493-539 fired EXACTLY two backend calls in the correct order: (i) POST /api/pros-cons/{id}/factors/reorder with alphabetical ordered_ids (Alpha, Mango, Banana, Echo, Zeta) → 200, (ii) PUT /api/pros-cons/{id}/config {"step7_alpha_seeded": true} → 200. UI rendered Mandatory: A1 Alpha, A2 Mango and Optional: B1 Banana, B2 Echo, B3 Zeta. After clicking ▼ on Banana, server priority_ranks updated to Alpha, Mango, Echo, Banana, Zeta and UI re-rendered as B1 Echo, B2 Banana, B3 Zeta. CRITICAL ASSERTION (f): after wiping localStorage AGAIN, navigating away to /tools/pros-cons, and returning to the wizard at Step 7 — order remained Echo, Banana, Zeta (NOT re-alphabetized), zero `/factors/reorder` or `/config` calls were made, and backend `step7_alpha_seeded` stayed true. Cross-device durability is now provably independent of browser localStorage. No backend or frontend defects observed in this scope.

critical_code_review_comments: Backend route update_config at /app/backend/routes/pros_cons.py:626-640 correctly persists `step7_alpha_seeded` as a top-level boolean on the analysis doc (outside the `config` blob) via the `extra` dict; bool(body[k]) is used to coerce. The response echoes both `config` and the extra flag, allowing the frontend to verify the persisted value. Implementation is symmetric to (and stated to mirror) the SWOT route.

Frontend useEffect at /app/frontend/app/tools/pros-cons-wizard.tsx:493-539 reads `analysis.step7_alpha_seeded === true` as the gate — strict equality avoids running the seed on undefined/null/false. After a successful POST /factors/reorder, it chains markSeeded() which calls PUT /config and then reload(), so the analysis object is refetched with the flag set, breaking the dependency loop on subsequent renders. Dependency array includes `(analysis as any)?.step7_alpha_seeded`, so the gate is re-evaluated when the flag changes.

Idempotent revisit path is preserved: when desired === currentMainsOrder, the code skips the reorder POST and calls markSeeded() directly — but this is only used when ranks already happen to be alphabetical AND the flag was somehow missed. Verified via network monitor that the second visit produced ZERO calls (the flag-true gate short-circuits before this branch).

Minor (non-blocking): the catch on /factors/reorder logs but does not set the flag, so a permanent ownership/4xx error would cause the seed effect to retry on every Step 7 entry. Acceptable for transient network errors. Same comment as iteration_5; not a regression.

rca_of_issue: No defect to root-cause — this was a verification pass for an architectural improvement (server-side persistence of the alphabetical-seed gate). The change closes the cross-device caveat raised in iteration_5 (localStorage was per-browser, so opening the analysis in a fresh browser could re-trigger the seed and overwrite manual reorders). With the new top-level boolean on the analysis doc, the seed effect short-circuits on `analysis.step7_alpha_seeded === true` regardless of client storage state — proven by the (e)→(f) sequence: after a complete localStorage wipe, the manually reordered Echo/Banana/Zeta order persisted and zero seed calls were emitted.
